extracted.intended_audience: USPTO examiners, patent prosecutors/attorneys, patent applicants
extracted.subtask_short: disqualifying commonly owned patent as prior art
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for using an affidavit/declaration and terminal disclaimer under 37 CFR 1.131(c) to disqualify a commonly owned U.S. patent or published application as prior art in pre-AIA rejections. Covers applicability, required papers, signer authority, and limits on effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editor note — inapplicability to first-inventor-to-file AIA applications
rubrics_metrics.description: This MPEP section is not applicable to applications subject to examination under the first inventor to file provisions of the AIA as explained in 35 U.S.C. 100 (note) and MPEP § 2159.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not apply 37 CFR 1.131(c) procedures to AIA first-inventor-to-file applications; the section and its procedures are limited to pre‑AIA contexts described elsewhere in the section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Situations when 37 CFR 1.131(c) may be invoked
rubrics_metrics.description: When any claim of an application or a patent under reexamination is rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as in effect on March 15, 2013, on a U.S. patent or U.S. patent application publication which is not prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(b) as in effect on March 15, 2013, and the inventions defined by the claims in the application or patent under reexamination and by the claims in the patent or published application are not identical but are not patentably distinct, and the inventions are owned by the same party, the applicant or owner of the patent under reexamination may disqualify the patent or patent application publication as prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All listed conditions must be present: (1) a pre‑AIA §103 rejection based on a U.S. patent/publication, (2) that reference is not prior art under pre‑AIA §102(b), (3) the two claim sets are not identical but not patentably distinct, and (4) common ownership. If any condition is missing, 1.131(c) does not apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required submissions to disqualify the commonly owned patent/publication
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent or patent application publication can be disqualified as prior art by submission of: (1) A terminal disclaimer in accordance with § 1.321(c); and (2) An oath or declaration stating that the application or patent under reexamination and patent or published application are currently owned by the same party, and that the inventor named in the application or patent under reexamination is the prior inventor under 35 U.S.C. 104 as in effect on March 15, 2013.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both documents are required together to invoke 1.131(c). The oath/declaration must include the ownership statement and the explicit assertion that the named inventor is the prior inventor under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 104 (as of March 15, 2013).

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer requirement and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: A terminal disclaimer in accordance with 37 CFR 1.321(c) is required to disqualify the commonly owned patent under 37 CFR 1.131(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A terminal disclaimer is effective only in overcoming a nonstatutory double patenting rejection and cannot be used to overcome statutory double patenting. See MPEP § 804, subsection I.B.2 for additional discussion. Prepare terminal disclaimer per §1.321(c) formalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oath/declaration substantive requirement — "prior inventor" under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 104
rubrics_metrics.description: The oath or declaration must state that the inventor named in the application or patent under reexamination is the prior inventor under 35 U.S.C. 104 as in effect on March 15, 2013.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The inventor named must have invented the claimed subject matter before the actual date of invention of the subject matter of the reference claims. The affidavit/declaration must make this showing; see related MPEP discussion on evidence of prior invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on establishing dates of invention in foreign countries
rubrics_metrics.description: The phrase 'prior inventor under 35 U.S.C. 104 as in effect on March 15, 2013' requires that the inventor named ... may not: (A) establish a date of invention in a foreign country other than a NAFTA or WTO member country; (B) establish a date of invention in a WTO member country other than a NAFTA country earlier than January 1, 1996; or (C) establish a date of invention in a NAFTA country other than the U.S. earlier than December 8, 1993.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When asserting an earlier date of invention under pre‑AIA §104, ensure the date and country of the acts relied upon satisfy these territorial and date limits. Acts outside permitted countries or before permitted dates will not satisfy the prior‑inventor requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability to applications/patents with pre‑AIA effective filing dates and certain priority references
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisions of this section apply to any application for patent, and to any patent issuing thereon, that contains, or contained at any time: (1) A claim to an invention that has an effective filing date as defined in § 1.109 that is before March 16, 2013; or (2) A specific reference under 35 U.S.C. 120, 121, 365(c), or 386(c) to any patent or application that contains, or contained at any time, a claim to an invention that has an effective filing date as defined in § 1.109 that is before March 16, 2013.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply 1.131(c) only to applications/patents that meet these effective filing date or priority‑reference conditions. If an application has no pre‑AIA effective filing date and no such references, 1.131(c) is not applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interaction with 37 CFR 1.130 and 35 U.S.C. 102(g)
rubrics_metrics.description: In an application for patent to which the provisions of § 1.130 apply, and to any patent issuing thereon, the provisions of this section are applicable only with respect to a rejection under 35 U.S.C. 102(g) as in effect on March 15, 2013.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When §1.130 (prior art exceptions under AIA provisions) applies to an application, limit the usage of 1.131(c) to pre‑AIA §102(g) style rejections as specified here; do not extend 1.131(c) beyond that narrow circumstance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipating references cannot be disqualified under 1.131(c)
rubrics_metrics.description: A U.S. patent or U.S. patent application publication that anticipates the claimed subject matter cannot be disqualified as prior art under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(c) or 37 CFR 1.131(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the reference constitutes anticipation (i.e., is prior art that fully discloses the claimed subject matter), 1.131(c) cannot be used to disqualify it; the rule applies only where the reference is not prior art under the cited pre‑AIA provisions and the inventions are not patentably distinct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit/declaration signatory authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The affidavit or declaration may be signed by the inventor(s), the attorney or agent of record, or assignee(s) of the entire interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure signatory has proper authority: assignee signatory must be assignee of the entire interest; attorneys/agents signing must be of record. Follow formal requirements for affidavits/declarations as discussed elsewhere in MPEP (see related sections on formal requirements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Relation to interference practice and antedating constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.131(c) addresses situations where the rejection ... is based on a U.S. patent or U.S. patent application publication which is not prior art under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(b) due to the requirement in 37 CFR 1.131(a) that any U.S. patent or U.S. patent application publication to be antedated not claim interfering subject matter (as defined in 37 CFR 41.203(a)). The applicant or patent owner is also prevented from proceeding in an interference due to the provision in 37 CFR 41.206 that an interference will not normally be declared or continued between applications that are commonly owned, or an application and an unexpired patent that are commonly owned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 1.131(c) only in the proper antedating/interference contexts; understand that antedating cannot be based on interfering subject matter and common ownership normally bars interference, which is a policy reason for the 1.131(c) procedures.
